The model works fine when I include covariates at site level or/and at point level. However, when I am trying to include a factor on the point level it won’t converge anymore. I can of course increase number of interations even more but as the n.eff I am getting for the factor levels are extremely low I assume I am making some other mistake.

messages.author: 4a635fe980c8c1cd
messages.subject: Re: Use of factors in baysien multi scale occupancy modelles
parts:
Hi Jenny,

Just stream of consciousness here (caveat emptor): am I off-base, or are these two models suggesting completely different effects of betaHab[1]? Is it possible there's some sort of confoundment between covariates for theta and psi (or alternatively, are the categories being used for theta all-inclusive...e.g., only three parameters are identifiable)? Other alternatives might include poor tuning of the jump parameters (see Mike Meredith's post below regarding adaptation vs. burn-in) and/or just getting stuck in a strange part of the parameter space [the prior for int.psi/theta makes me a little uneasy. You certainly seem to have enough data to escape any prior; but you're putting tremendous prior weight on intercept values that are less than .01 or greater than .99 on the probability scale...maybe the standard int.theta~U(0,1), beta0.beta<-inv.logit(int.theta) back-transform would work well here]?  I feel as through trace-plots might give you a sense of whether this is a data issue or an algorithmic/prior issue...are the samples of specific parameters completely correlated, or taking a long time to move towards a stationary distribution, or getting stuck frequently, or some combination there-of (etc.)?  

John

messages.author: 527d9b3ec7deff2d
messages.subject: Re: Use of factors in baysien multi scale occupancy modelles
parts:
I agree with John that the priors for the probability intercepts are poorly specified here.  A uniform prior on the probability scale that is then transformed to the logit would be better.  This is particularly true for the means parameterization (version #2) where all 4 factor estimates represent logit-transformed probabilities.  If you want a quick fix, try this:

for(m in 1:4){
  betaHab[m] ~ dnorm(0, 0.37)
}

This tau (0.37) gives you a probability prior with mostly uniform support from 0 to 1.
